entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__get_thread
entries.description:
Retrieves a specific email thread from the authenticated user's Gmail account, including its `viewUrl` and a list of its messages (each with their own `viewUrl`).

Note: This tool does not support retrieving drafts. Any draft messages within a thread are omitted. To view drafts, use the `list_drafts` tool instead.

The optional `messageFormat` parameter controls the format of the messages returned. By default (or with `FULL_CONTENT`), it returns the full content of messages. We recommend using `PLAIN_TEXT`, which returns the plain text body without the HTML body. Use `MINIMAL` to include only subject and snippet (excluding body). Use `METADATA_ONLY` to include only basic metadata (message ID, thread ID, viewUrl, labels, timestamp, and size estimate).

messageFormat.description: Optional. Specifies the format of the messages returned within the thread. Defaults to `FULL_CONTENT`. We recommend using `PLAIN_TEXT` to prevent context exhaustion. Note: `MINIMAL` format returns `id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`. `METADATA_ONLY` format returns `id`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`. `FULL_CONTENT` returns `id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`, `attachment_ids`, `plaintext_body`, `html_body`, `attachments`. `PLAIN_TEXT` returns `id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`, `attachment_ids`, `plaintext_body`, `attachments` (without `html_body`). `RAW` format is not supported here.
x-google-enum-descriptions: Returns all message fields (`id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`, `attachment_ids`, `plaintext_body`, `html_body`, `attachments`, `view_url`) if applicable.

Returns all information in `MINIMAL` plus `plaintext_body`, `attachment_ids`, and `attachments` (if applicable). If plain text body is not available, converts the HTML body to plain text/markdown. Omits `html_body`.
Returns the raw MIME message content.

threadId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the thread to fetch.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__search_threads
entries.description:
Lists email threads from the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool can filter threads based on a query string and supports pagination. It returns a list of threads, including their IDs, `viewUrl`, and related messages (each with their own `viewUrl`). Each related message contains details like a snippet of the message body, the subject, the sender, the recipients etc. The `view` parameter controls which fields are populated in the related messages. By default (or with `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`), it includes subject and snippet. Use `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` to exclude subject and snippet. Note that the full message bodies are not returned by this tool; use the 'get_thread' tool with a thread ID to fetch the full message body if needed. Threads with excluded criteria may still appear in the results. This occurs because Gmail identifies matching messages first. For example, if you search for -is:starred, Gmail will find an entire thread if it contains at least one unstarred message, even if other emails in that same conversation are starred.

To list threads in a specific inbox category tab, use the `category:` operator with `primary`, `social`, `promotions`, `updates`, or `forums` (e.g. `in:inbox category:promotions`).

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

includeTrash.description: Optional. Include threads from TRASH in the results. Defaults to false.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of threads to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list. Leave empty to fetch the first page. This is primarily used for pagination to continue fetching results from where the previous `SearchThreads` call left off, especially when the number of threads matching the query exceeds the `page_size` limit.

query.description: Optional. A query string to filter the threads. Natural language queries must be pre-converted into Gmail syntax queries to use this tool. If omitted, all threads (excluding spam and trash by default) are listed. Supported Operators by Category: Sender & Recipient: - `from:` — Sent from a specific person. - `to:` — Sent to a specific person. - `cc:` — Specific people in Cc. - `bcc:` — Specific people in Bcc. - `deliveredto:` — Delivered to a specific address. - `list:` — From a specific mailing list. Time & Date: - `after:YYYY/MM/DD` / `newer:YYYY/MM/DD` — Received after a date. - `before:YYYY/MM/DD` / `older:YYYY/MM/DD` — Received before a date. - `older_than:` — Older than a duration (for example, `1y`, `2d`). - `newer_than:` — Newer than a duration. Content: - `subject:` — Words in the subject line. - `has:` — Has specific content types (attachment, drive, youtube, document). - `filename:` — Attachment with a specific name or type. - `""` — Search for an exact word or phrase. (for example, `"holiday"`, `"holiday vacation"`). Note: Double quotes enforce strict contiguous phrase matching. For topic, discussion, or keyword queries, prefer unquoted keywords (e.g. `partner advertising` instead of `"partner advertising"`). - `+` — Match a word exactly. (for example, `+holiday`, `+unicorn`) - `rfc822msgid:` — Specific message ID header. - `AROUND ` — Find words near each other (for example, `holiday AROUND 10 vacation`). Labels & Categories: - `label:` — Under a specific label. The tool accepts label IDs, not display names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the ID. - `category:` — In a category (primary, social, promotions, updates, forums, reservations, purchases). - `in:` — Search in specific labels (archive, snoozed, trash, sent, inbox). For example, `in:trash`, `in:inbox`. Archived and sent messages are included by default; use `-in:archive` and `-in:sent` to exclude them. Drafts are explicitly excluded by default by the tool. Use `in:inbox` to restrict search to the inbox only. - `has:userlabels` — Has any user labels. - `has:nouserlabels` — Does not have any user labels. - `has:*-star` — Specific star colors (if enabled, for example, `has:yellow-star`). - `in:draft` — Search in drafts. -in:draft means exclude drafts from the search results. - `in:sent` — Search in sent messages. - `in:anywhere` — Search in all folders (including spam and trash). Status: - `is:` — Search by status (important, starred, unread, read, muted). Size: - `size:` — Specific size in bytes. - `larger:` / `smaller:` — Larger or smaller than a size (for example, `10M` for 10 MB). Logic & Grouping: - `AND` — Match all criteria (default behavior). - `OR` or `{ }` — Match one or more criteria (for example, `from:amy OR from:david`, `{from:amy from:david}`). - `-` (minus) — Exclude criteria (for example, `-movie`). - `( )` — Group multiple search terms (for example, `subject:(dinner film)`). Examples: - `subject:OneMCP Update` - `from:user@example.com` - `to:user2@example.com AND newer_than:7d` - `project proposal has:attachment` - `is:unread -in:draft` To prevent overly strict queries, favor concise, keyword-based queries over long subject strings or full sentences. Avoid copying overly detailed subjects from the user prompt verbatim, as this often leads to search misses. Instead, extract the most unique keywords (e.g., subject:amazon \"delivery\" OR \"order\" instead of \"amazon order\"). Use boolean operators to broaden your search coverage. Use OR to search for synonyms or multiple potential senders, and use ( ) for grouping criteria. Note that whitespace between terms acts as an implicit AND.

view.description: Optional. Controls the fields populated for threads in the thread list. Defaults to `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`. `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL` returns `id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`. `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` returns `id`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`.

# NeatLogs Public API - Traces and Spans Endpoints

## Base URL
`https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public`

(EU: `https://eu.app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public`)

## Authentication
All requests require a Bearer token in the Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer <service-account-token>
```

## Project Context
Requests use the `x-project-id` header to specify the project:
```
x-project-id: <project-uuid>
```

## Key Details

**Authentication Credential**: Service account tokens are used for API access, not project keys.

**Response Format**: Per the documentation, "JSON success responses contain `success: true`, a server-generated `requestId`, and `data`."

**Pagination**: The API uses cursor-based pagination for list operations.

## For Specific Endpoints

The documentation references "all **285 operations** in the deployed Public API contract" but doesn't explicitly list individual trace/span endpoints in the provided content. You'll need to:

1. Visit the [Endpoint reference](/api-reference/endpoints) section
2. Look under the "Traces" category in the Reference menu
3. Download the [OpenAPI JSON specification](/openapi/public-api.json) for complete method, path, and parameter details

This will provide exact paths, HTTP methods, query parameters, and response schemas for all trace and span operations.

"""
Neatlogs SDK - Simple, powerful LLM observability.
Primary API:
    - init(), flush(), shutdown() - Lifecycle management
    - @span(kind="...") - Universal decorator for custom code instrumentation
    - trace() - Context manager for prompt tracking and session management
    - SystemPromptTemplate - Structured prompt versioning (formerly PromptTemplate)
Quick Start:
    >>> from neatlogs import init, span, trace, SystemPromptTemplate
    >>>

    - "AGENT" - Agent execution

def wrap_openai_client(client: Any) -> Any:
    """
    Wrap an OpenAI client instance. Returns the same client with all
    LLM-relevant resources patched to auto-trace.
    """
    _safe(_patch_completions, _resource(client, "chat", "completions"))
    _safe(_patch_chat_parse, _resource(client, "chat", "completions"), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_legacy_completions, getattr(client, "completions", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_responses, getattr(client, "responses", None))
    _safe(_patch_responses_parse, getattr(client, "responses", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_embeddings, getattr(client, "embeddings", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_images, getattr(client, "images", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_audio, getattr(client, "audio", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_moderations, getattr(client, "moderations", None), sync=True)
    _safe(_patch_batches, getattr(client, "batches", None), sync=True)
    # beta.chat.completions.parse
    beta = getattr(client, "beta", None)
    if beta is not None:
        _safe(_patch_chat_parse, _resource(beta, "chat", "completions"), sync=True)
    return client

"""Expense-auditor agent: converts a trip's receipts to USD, totals them, and flags policy violations."""
import json

import neatlogs

from agent_doctor.llm import PATIENT_MODEL, get_client
from patient.tools import TOOL_FUNCTIONS, TOOL_SCHEMAS

MAX_STEPS = 12

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an expense auditor. For the receipts you are given:
1. Convert every item to USD using get_exchange_rate (multiply the amount by the rate).
2. Use calculate for all arithmetic.
3. Run check_policy on every item.
4. When done, reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose:
   {"total_usd": <number rounded to 2 decimals>, "violations": [<category of each item over its limit>]}"""


@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
def audit_expenses(receipts: str) -> dict:
    client = get_client()
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": receipts}]

    for _ in range(MAX_STEPS):
        response = client.chat.completions.create(model=PATIENT_MODEL, messages=messages, tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS)
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        messages.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))

        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return parse_report(msg.content)

        for call in msg.tool_calls:
            args = json.loads(call.function.arguments)
            result = TOOL_FUNCTIONS[call.function.name](**args)
            messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": json.dumps(result)})

    raise RuntimeError(f"agent did not finish within {MAX_STEPS} steps")


def parse_report(text: str) -> dict:
    data = json.loads(text.strip().removeprefix("```json").removesuffix("```"))
    return {"total": float(data["total"]), "violations": sorted(data["violations"])}

"""Run the patient's test suite. Every case is one neatlogs trace, grouped by --session.

    python -m patient.run --session exam-123 --out results.json
"""
import argparse
import json
import traceback

import neatlogs

from patient.agent import audit_expenses
from patient.cases import CASES, grade


def run_case(case: dict, session: str) -> dict:
    with neatlogs.trace(f"expense-audit:{case['id']}", session_id=session, case_id=case["id"]):
        try:
            report = audit_expenses(case["receipts"])
            passed, reason = grade(report, case["expected"])
            return {"id": case["id"], "passed": passed, "reason": reason, "output": report}
        except Exception as e:
            return {
                "id": case["id"],
                "passed": False,
                "reason": f"crashed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}",
                "traceback": traceback.format_exc(limit=6),
            }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--case", help="run a single case id")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cases = [c for c in CASES if not args.case or c["id"] == args.case]
    results = [run_case(c, args.session) for c in cases]
    neatlogs.flush()

    for r in results:
        print(f"{'PASS' if r['passed'] else 'FAIL'}  {r['id']:<18} {r['reason']}")
    print(f"{sum(r['passed'] for r in results)}/{len(results)} passed")
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w") as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    python -m patient.run --session exam-123 --out results.json
"""
import argparse
import json
import traceback

import neatlogs

from patient.agent import audit_expenses
from patient.cases import CASES, grade


def run_case(case: dict, session: str) -> dict:
    with neatlogs.trace(f"expense-audit:{case['id']}", session_id=session, case_id=case["id"]):
        try:
            report = audit_expenses(case["receipts"])
            passed, reason = grade(report, case["expected"])
            return {"id": case["id"], "passed": passed, "reason": reason, "output": report}
        except Exception as e:
            return {
                "id": case["id"],
                "passed": False,
                "reason": f"crashed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}",
                "traceback": traceback.format_exc(limit=6),
            }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--case", help="run a single case id")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cases = [c for c in CASES if not args.case or c["id"] == args.case]
    results = [run_case(c, args.session) for c in cases]
    neatlogs.flush()

    for r in results:
        print(f"{'PASS' if r['passed'] else 'FAIL'}  {r['id']:<18} {r['reason']}")
    print(f"{sum(r['passed'] for r in results)}/{len(results)} passed")
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w") as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Agent Doctor: examines a failing agent through its neatlogs traces, patches it, and proves the fix."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from agent_doctor import ui
from agent_doctor.llm import DOCTOR_MODEL, ROOT, get_client
from agent_doctor.neatlogs_api import NeatlogsAPI

PATIENT_DIR = ROOT / "patient"
# Ground truth and the test harness are off limits: the Doctor fixes the agent, not the exam.
PROTECTED = {"patient/cases.py", "patient/run.py"}
MAX_TRACE_CHARS = 7000
MAX_TRACES_PER_ROUND = 3

DOCTOR_PROMPT = """You are Agent Doctor, an expert at debugging LLM agents from their execution traces.

You get: the agent's source code, its test results, and neatlogs traces of the failing runs
(every LLM call, tool call, arguments, outputs and exceptions).

Find the ROOT CAUSE of the failures. Ground every claim in the traces: quote the span, tool
arguments or error that proves it. Fix the agent's code, never the tests. Prefer the smallest
change that fixes the root cause. Failures can be layered: a crash may hide a logic bug that only
shows once the crash is fixed, so fix what the evidence supports and keep tool contracts consistent.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object:
{
  "diagnosis": "<one-line headline of the bug>",
  "root_cause": "<2-4 sentences explaining why the agent fails>",
  "evidence": ["<quote or fact from a trace>", ...],
  "edits": [{"file": "patient/<file>.py", "find": "<exact unique snippet>", "replace": "<new snippet>"}]
}
Each "find" must match the current file exactly once, including whitespace."""


@dataclass
class Exam:
    session: str
    results: list[dict]
    traces: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def passed(self) -> int:
        return sum(r["passed"] for r in self.results)

    @property
    def crashes(self) -> int:
        return sum(r["reason"].startswith("crashed") for r in self.results)

    @property
    def score(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.passed, -self.crashes)

    def totals(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "tokens": sum(t.get("totalTokens") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "cost": sum(t.get("totalCostUsd") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "llm_calls": sum(t.get("llmCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "tool_calls": sum(t.get("toolCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),
        }


class Doctor:
    def __init__(self, max_rounds: int = 4, open_pr: bool = True):
        self.client = get_client()
        self.api = NeatlogsAPI()
        self.max_rounds = max_rounds
        self.open_pr = open_pr
        self.stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
        self.branch = f"doctor/heal-{self.stamp}"
        self.run_dir = ROOT / ".doctor_runs" / self.stamp
        self.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.history: list[dict] = []

    # ---- examination -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL")
    def examine(self, label: str) -> Exam:
        session = f"exam-{self.stamp}-{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:4]}"
        out = self.run_dir / f"{label}.json"
        ui.step(f"Examining patient  [dim](session {session})[/]")
        subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "patient.run", "--session", session, "--out", str(out)],
            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
        )
        exam = Exam(session, json.loads(out.read_text()))
        ui.step("Pulling traces from neatlogs")
        exam.traces = self.api.session_traces(session, expected=len(exam.results))
        ui.exam_table(exam)
        return exam

    def trace_evidence(self, exam: Exam) -> str:
        """Export the failing runs' traces from neatlogs as the Doctor's primary evidence."""
        by_case = {t.get("traceName", "").split(":", 1)[-1]: t for t in exam.traces}
        sections = []
        for r in [r for r in exam.results if not r["passed"]][:MAX_TRACES_PER_ROUND]:
            trace = by_case.get(r["id"])
            if not trace:
                sections.append(f"### case {r['id']}: no trace found in neatlogs")
                continue
            md = self.api.export_markdown(trace["traceId"])
            if len(md) > MAX_TRACE_CHARS:
                md = md[: MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2] + "\n...[truncated]...\n" + md[-MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2 :]
            sections.append(f"### case {r['id']} - trace {trace['traceId']} (status {trace.get('status')})\n{md}")
        return "\n\n".join(sections)

    # ---- diagnosis & treatment ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
    def diagnose(self, exam: Exam) -> dict:
        ui.step(f"Diagnosing with {DOCTOR_MODEL}")
        sources = "\n\n".join(
            f"=== {p.relative_to(ROOT)} ===\n{p.read_text()}"
            for p in sorted(PATIENT_DIR.glob("*.py"))
            if str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) not in PROTECTED and p.name != "__init__.py"
        )
        results = json.dumps([{k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != "traceback"} for r in exam.results], indent=1)
        history = json.dumps(self.history, indent=1) if self.history else "none"
        user = (
            f"## Agent source\n{sources}\n\n## Test results\n{results}\n\n"
            f"## Previous treatment rounds\n{history}\n\n## neatlogs traces of failing runs\n{self.trace_evidence(exam)}"
        )
        response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=DOCTOR_MODEL,
            messages=[{"role": "system", "content": DOCTOR_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
            max_tokens=4000,
        )
        text = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        text = text[text.find("{") : text.rfind("}") + 1]
        plan = json.loads(text)
        ui.diagnosis(plan)
        return plan

    def apply(self, edits: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
        """Apply find/replace edits; everything is validated before any file is written."""
        pending: dict[Path, str] = {}
        for e in edits:
            if e["file"] in PROTECTED or not e["file"].startswith("patient/"):
                raise ValueError(f"refusing to edit {e['file']}")
            path = ROOT / e["file"]
            text = pending.get(path, path.read_text())
            if text.count(e["find"]) != 1:
                raise ValueError(f"'find' snippet matched {text.count(e['find'])} times in {e['file']}")
            pending[path] = text.replace(e["find"], e["replace"])
        for path, text in pending.items():
            path.write_text(text)
        ui.patch(edits)
        return [str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) for p in pending]

    def revert(self, files: list[str]):
        subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "--", *files], cwd=ROOT, check=True)

    def commit(self, plan: dict, files: list[str], before: Exam, after: Exam):
        msg = (
            f"Doctor: {plan['diagnosis']}\n\n{plan['root_cause']}\n\n"
            f"Tests: {before.passed}/{len(before.results)} -> {after.passed}/{len(after.results)} passing\n"
            f"Evidence session: {before.session}\nVerified in session: {after.session}"
        )
        git(["add", *files])
        git(["commit", "-m", msg])

    # ---- main loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")
    def heal(self) -> dict:
        ui.banner()
        start_branch = git(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"]).strip()
        if git(["status", "--porcelain", "patient"]).strip():
            raise RuntimeError("patient/ has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first")
        git(["checkout", "-b", self.branch])

        first = current = self.examine("intake")
        round_no = 0
        while current.passed < len(current.results) and round_no < self.max_rounds:
            round_no += 1
            ui.round_header(round_no, self.max_rounds)
            try:
                plan = self.diagnose(current)
                files = self.apply(plan["edits"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
                ui.warn(f"Treatment plan unusable: {e}")
                self.history.append({"round": round_no, "error": str(e)})
                continue

            after = self.examine(f"round{round_no}")
            outcome = {
                "round": round_no, "diagnosis": plan["diagnosis"], "files": files,
                "before": f"{current.passed}/{len(current.results)}", "after": f"{after.passed}/{len(after.results)}",
                "after_failures": [r["reason"] for r in after.results if not r["passed"]],
            }
            if after.score > current.score:
                self.commit(plan, files, current, after)
                ui.ok(f"Improvement verified in traces: {outcome['before']} -> {outcome['after']}. Committed.")
                outcome["kept"] = True
                current = after
            else:
                self.revert(files)
                ui.warn(f"No improvement ({outcome['before']} -> {outcome['after']}). Patch reverted.")
                outcome["kept"] = False
            self.history.append(outcome)

        report = self.write_report(first, current)
        if any(h.get("kept") for h in self.history) and self.open_pr:
            self.publish(report, first, current)
        else:
            git(["checkout", start_branch])
        ui.summary(first, current)
        return {"before": first.passed, "after": current.passed, "branch": self.branch}

    # ---- reporting ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def write_report(self, first: Exam, last: Exam) -> Path:
        b, a = first.totals(), last.totals()
        lines = [
            f"# Agent Doctor report - {self.stamp}",
            "",
            f"**Result:** {first.passed}/{len(first.results)} -> **{last.passed}/{len(last.results)}** test cases passing",
            "",
            "| | Before | After |",
            "|---|---|---|",
            f"| Passing cases | {first.passed}/{len(first.results)} | {last.passed}/{len(last.results)} |",
            f"| Crashes | {first.crashes} | {last.crashes} |",
            f"| LLM calls | {b['llm_calls']} | {a['llm_calls']} |",
            f"| Tool calls | {b['tool_calls']} | {a['tool_calls']} |",
            f"| Tokens | {b['tokens']} | {a['tokens']} |",
            "",
            f"neatlogs sessions: before `{first.session}`, after `{last.session}`",
            "",
            "## Treatment log",
        ]
        for h in self.history:
            if "error" in h:
                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: plan rejected ({h['error']})")
            else:
                verdict = "kept" if h["kept"] else "reverted"
                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: **{h['diagnosis']}** ({h['before']} -> {h['after']}, {verdict})")
        path = ROOT / "reports" / f"heal-{self.stamp}.md"
        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        git(["add", str(path.relative_to(ROOT))])
        git(["commit", "-m", f"Doctor: add healing report {self.stamp}"])
        return path

    def publish(self, report: Path, first: Exam, last: Exam):
        ui.step(f"Pushing {self.branch} and opening a pull request")

MAX_TRACES_PER_ROUND = 3

arguments or error that proves it. Fix the agent's code, never the tests. Prefer the smallest

{

  "evidence": ["<quote or fact from a trace>", ...],

    def crashes(self) -> int:

    def score(self) -> tuple[int, int]:

    def totals(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "tokens": sum(t.get("totalTokens") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "cost": sum(t.get("totalCostUsd") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "llm_calls": sum(t.get("llmCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "tool_calls": sum(t.get("toolCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),

                continue

            if len(md) > MAX_TRACE_CHARS:
                md = md[: MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2] + "\n...[truncated]...\n" + md[-MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2 :]

            f"Evidence session: {before.session}\nVerified in session: {after.session}"

        if git(["status", "--porcelain", "patient"]).strip():

            round_no += 1
            ui.round_header(round_no, self.max_rounds)
            try:

                self.history.append({"round": round_no, "error": str(e)})
                continue

            outcome = {
                "round": round_no, "diagnosis": plan["diagnosis"], "files": files,
                "before": f"{current.passed}/{len(current.results)}", "after": f"{after.passed}/{len(after.results)}",
                "after_failures": [r["reason"] for r in after.results if not r["passed"]],

                self.commit(plan, files, current, after)
                ui.ok(f"Improvement verified in traces: {outcome['before']} -> {outcome['after']}. Committed.")

            else:

            "",
            "| | Before | After |",
            "|---|---|---|",
            f"| Passing cases | {first.passed}/{len(first.results)} | {last.passed}/{len(last.results)} |",
            f"| Crashes | {first.crashes} | {last.crashes} |",
            f"| LLM calls | {b['llm_calls']} | {a['llm_calls']} |",
            f"| Tool calls | {b['tool_calls']} | {a['tool_calls']} |",
            f"| Tokens | {b['tokens']} | {a['tokens']} |",
            "",
            f"neatlogs sessions: before `{first.session}`, after `{last.session}`",
            "",
            "## Treatment log",
        ]
        for h in self.history:
            if "error" in h:
                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: plan rejected ({h['error']})")
            else:

                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: **{h['diagnosis']}** ({h['before']} -> {h['after']}, {verdict})")

        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        git(["add", str(path.relative_to(ROOT))])
        git(["commit", "-m", f"Doctor: add healing report {self.stamp}"])
        return path

    def publish(self, report: Path, first: Exam, last: Exam):
        ui.step(f"Pushing {self.branch} and opening a pull request")
        git(["push", "-u", "origin", self.branch])
        title = f"Agent Doctor: patient healed ({first.passed}/{len(first.results)} -> {last.passed}/{len(last.results)})"
        body = report.read_text() + "\n\n🤖 Opened autonomously by Agent Doctor"
        pr = subprocess.run(
            ["gh", "pr", "create", "--head", self.branch, "--title", title, "--body", body],

        )
        ui.ok(f"Pull request: {pr.stdout.strip()}" if pr.returncode == 0 else f"PR failed: {pr.stderr.strip()}")

    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

content.text:
Steps 1–4 are built and pushed (2 commits on `main`). One thing is blocking me.

## Blocked: I need the second neatlogs key
Sending traces works, but reading them back returns `401 Unauthorized`, and the Doctor needs to read them. The key in your `.env` is the one for sending traces. The neatlogs **Settings → API keys** page shows two keys, and the read API needs the **other one** (the "public API key").

Add these two lines to `.env`:
```
NEATLOGS_PUBLIC_API_KEY=<the other key on that page>
NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID=<project UUID, if the page shows one; it's optional>
```
If there's no second key, look for "Service accounts" in the neatlogs settings, create one with read access to the project, and put its `nlsa_...` token in `NEATLOGS_PUBLIC_API_KEY`.

While you're in the dashboard, check the **Traces tab**. You should see 4 traces named `expense-audit:*` that failed with `KeyError`. That's the patient being sick, so it's working as intended.

## What's built
- **Patient** ([patient/](patient/)): an expense-auditor agent on `claude-haiku` with 3 planted bugs that stack on top of each other:
  1. Its tool schema says `meal`/`hotel`/`taxi`, but the policy table uses `meals`/`lodging`/`transport`, so it crashes with a `KeyError`.
  2. The exchange rate is inverted, so the totals come out wildly wrong. This only shows up once bug 1 is fixed.
  3. The prompt asks for `total_usd`, but the parser reads `total`, so it fails while parsing the output.

  Right now it passes **0 of 4 test cases**.
- **Doctor** ([agent_doctor/doctor.py](agent_doctor/doctor.py)), on `claude-sonnet-4.6`, runs this loop:
  1. Run the patient's tests.
  2. Pull and export the failing traces from neatlogs.
  3. Diagnose the problem, quoting the traces as evidence.
  4. Patch the code. It isn't allowed to touch the test files.
  5. Run the tests again.
  6. Keep the patch and commit it if the results improved; otherwise undo it and try again.
  7. Push the branch, write a before/after report, and open a PR.

  Its own reasoning is traced in neatlogs too, and the terminal output is formatted for the demo.

Once the key is in, I'll run `python -m agent_doctor heal` from start to finish and fix whatever breaks.

One more thing about Entire: its hooks for Claude Code are installed, but it shows 0 checkpoints so far. My guess is that it saves them when my turn ends. I'll check it after this turn.

## 📣 Post #1 for X (post now)
> Day 2 of #neatHack 🛠️
>
> Building **Agent Doctor**: an AI agent that fixes other AI agents.
>
> It reads a broken agent's traces in @neatlogs, diagnoses the root cause, patches the code, re-runs it, and only keeps the fix if the traces prove it worked. Then it opens the PR itself.
>
> Our patient is already sick: 0/4 tests passing 🤒 Treatment starts tonight.
>
> Repo: github.com/bhargava-sarma/agent-doctor

Attach a screenshot of the failing traces from the neatlogs dashboard. A picture makes the post land much better.
